observations.behavior: Adds a guard that refuses to evaluate cohort filters when the database preparation of person properties has not run.
observations.posthog_connection: This prevents incorrect flag matching for users whose identity and property state are still pending. It also records an error and increments a counter rather than silently returning false or guessing.

observations.behavior: Adds a regression test asserting that NOT_IN cohort conditions fail closed when person-property DB prep never ran.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides evidence that the new failure path is exercised and does not grant flags incorrectly under missing-prep conditions.

review.reason: This chunk implements a substantive correctness improvement for PostHog's Rust feature-flag matching engine by adding an explicit guard against unsafe cohort evaluations during database preparation failures. It also includes documentation updates and a targeted regression test. This qualifies as Tier 2 because it establishes a reliable boundary around flag evaluation and prevents potential false-positive matches while remaining localized within the existing component. There is no clear Tier 3 systemic risk reduction; the change does not span multiple unrelated subsystems nor demonstrate recovery of previously lost functionality beyond this specific edge case.
review.posthog_relevance: Relevant to reliability and query correctness for users relying on cohort-based feature flags. Prevents incorrect entitlement decisions when identity properties have not been cached yet.
review.uncertainty: The exact production frequency of the guarded condition cannot be established from this patch alone; however, the presence of an error log and counter suggests awareness of a real failure mode rather than purely hypothetical protection.
